guidelines.detail: refines EVT-14 (The validator rejects the name attribute on messageEventDefinition (V-L1, line 20). The description (S2) notifies outside parties and gathers information from companies, so message events with names are needed. EVT-14 already states the messageRef placement, but it does not say where the name goes, so the schema violation can recur. The guideline does not contradict COL-06 because it applies when )

refines ACT-02 (The generated model uses userTask for three human steps with no mentioned software: 'Select leave model' (X1), 'Collect relevant information' (X2), and 'Gather information from companies' (X3). The reference models the corresponding steps as manualTasks (M4, M5, M7, M8). The description names no system for any of these steps, so the task type, not the presence of the activity, is the divergence. T)

Most missing elements (employer confirmation, financial support fetch and application, document check, end event 'return to job') are not stated in the description, so the reference adds content rather than reflecting a described structure. The reference's manualTask for the leave period conflicts with the earlier learned guideline that a stated waiting period is an intermediate catch event, so I cannot adopt that part. The one described structural point, parallel branches for unordered activities, is already covered by LRN-011 and LRN-010. No new guideline is supported by these records.

refines ACT-04 (The generated receiveTask for gathering information from companies (X2) models a waiting step, while the description describes work performed to collect information. The reference uses a different task type for this performed work. The related reference service task awaiting an employer confirmation (M1) shows the same confusion between waiting and performing work. A rule that separates performed )

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description has a message exchanged with an outside party, such as a notice sent to an outside body or information gathered from an outside party, and the modeled message event needs a name: Model the message event with a bpmn:message element that carries the name, and reference it from the event definition through messageRef. Do not put a name attribute on the bpmn:messageEventDefinition, since the BPMN 2.0.2 schema does not allow it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description has a message exchanged with an outside party, such as a notice sent to an outside body or information gathered from an outside party, and the modeled message event needs a name

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a human step, such as choosing among options or collecting or gathering information, and mentions no software, system, form, or online tool for performing it: Model that step as a bpmn:manualTask labelled with the description's own verb and object, not as a bpmn:userTask. Reserve bpmn:userTask for steps the description says are carried out with a software application.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a human step, such as choosing among options or collecting or gathering information, and mentions no software, system, form, or online tool for performing it

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity together with its recipient, its completion endpoint, or a second action coordinated with it (for example 'generates ... and sends it to the recipient', or 'sends ... to the recipient', or 'monitors ... until a stated condition'): Name the task so that its label keeps every element the description attaches to that activity: the recipient, the endpoint or completion condition, and any coordinated second action. Use the description's verbs and the qualifiers it states, and do not shorten the label to a bare verb-object pair that drops them. Keep the label short, but do not remove a stated part of the action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names an activity with an action verb and an object, and adds a qualifier to it such as a deadline, the kind of information involved, or the scope of the choice

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists an activity in which information is obtained from an external party as work the process performs, and does not say that the process waits for an incoming message or signal: Model this activity as a task performed by the responsible actor (manualTask or userTask), not as a receiveTask. Reserve receiveTask for a step the description explicitly presents as waiting for an incoming message.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists an activity in which information is obtained from an external party as work the process performs, and does not say that the process waits for an incoming message or signal
